column4: Visit note | 2026-07-07 04:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Sharmin Siddique, 45, female. Mrs. Siddique reports experiencing persistent head discomfort accompanied by neck tightness after spending long hours looking at a screen. She mentions that this issue began after a stressful house move to Bogura. She works as a beautician. Her medical history includes Hypothyroidism. She denies any vision changes, weakness, or numbness. On examination: pain score 3/10, BP 110/80 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 65 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and neck movements show mild muscle stiffness. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-08-29 09:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Salma Haque, 23, female. Ms. Haque explains that she suffers from severe menstrual pain accompanied by nausea, which frequently causes her to miss daily activities. She notes that her symptoms became worse since a stressful family move to Lalbagh. She works as a homemaker. She has no known comorbidities. She denies heavy bleeding or fever. On examination: pain score 9/10, BP 124/81 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 89 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with no acute tenderness outside of menstrual cramping. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2026-09-01 11:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Sohel Haque, 23, male. Mr. Haque complains of spots on his back, pimples and blackheads on his face, and marks left after pimples. He states that his skin condition became worse since working in a hot kitchen in Jatrabari. He works as a delivery rider. He has no known comorbidities. He denies any systemic symptoms or joint pains. On examination: about 23 inflamed spots on the face, BP 134/78 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 91 kg. Skin shows scattered papules and comedones across the facial and upper back regions. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.
